claims.claim: An acknowledgment or promise offered as evidence of a new or continuing contract must be in a writing signed by the party to be charged, subject to the payment rule stated next.
claims.quote: No acknowledgment or promise is sufficient evidence of a new or continuing contract, by which to take the case out of the operation of this title, unless the same is contained in some writing, signed by the party to be charged thereby,
claims.note: This is a necessary condition for relying on the writing, not a statement that any signed document suffices.

claims.claim: A payment by the party to be charged on principal or interest due on a promissory note counts as an acknowledgment or promise of a continuing contract.
claims.quote: any payment on account of principal or interest due on a promissory note made by the party to be charged shall be deemed a sufficient acknowledgment or promise of a continuing contract
claims.note: The payment rule is specific to promissory notes.

claims.claim: Each such payment stops the running of time for an action on the note and starts a new period.
claims.quote: to stop, from time to time as any such payment is made, the running of the time within which an action may be commenced upon the principal sum or upon any installment of principal or interest due on such note, and to start the running of a new period of time
claims.note: The covered amounts are the principal sum and installments of principal or interest.

claims.claim: Such a payment by itself does not revive an already barred cause of action.
claims.quote: but no such payment of itself shall revive a cause of action once barred.

claims.claim: The period for an action on a written instrument is four years.
claims.quote:
Within four years:
(a) An action upon any contract, obligation or liability founded upon an instrument in writing, except as provided in Section 336a;
claims.note: Four years is the general rule. Subdivision (a) also caps the period at three months after sale for the specified balance-due action following exercise of a power of sale.

flags.text: The four-year statement omits the Section 336a exception and the three-month post-sale cap in §337(a).
The draft does not state §337(d)’s prohibition on collection suits, arbitration, or other legal proceedings once the §337 period has run, or its limitation of extensions to §360.

The distinction between an approaching deadline and an expired one matters: a qualifying note payment before expiration can start a new period and weaken a limitations defense. The payment-alone nonrevival rule does not establish the effect of signing a payment plan or acknowledgment.

result.summary: Section 360 supports the signed-writing and promissory-note payment claims. Section 337(a) supports four years as a general period, not an unconditional deadline.
